noaaWeatherRadio.transmitterLocation: Providence Forge, VA (New Kent County area); served by NWS Wakefield
noaaWeatherRadio.notes: NWS Service Change Notice 24-57 (May 21, 2024) says broadcasts began June 21, 2024 and that KAE42 broadcasts forecasts/warnings for Henrico (SAME 051087), City of Richmond (051760), Hanover (051085), Charles City (051036), New Kent (051127) and others. This is the only transmitter in the sources opened that explicitly lists Henrico. Program SAME 051087 for Henrico alerts.

noaaWeatherRadio.transmitterLocation: Richmond area (NWS Wakefield table: 'Piedmont Region including the City of Richmond')
noaaWeatherRadio.notes: Listed on the NWS Wakefield NWR page at 162.475 MHz. That page does not name Henrico County explicitly, and its county table did not load, so Henrico coverage by WXK65 is likely but not confirmed from a source I opened. Try both 162.475 and 162.500 and keep whichever is stronger at home.

broadcastEAS.notes: Richmond Extended operational area LP-1 per Virginia State EAS Plan (dated 11-21-25), Facility ID 11963, first alerting source WRXL. Top 40 'Q94'; transmitter on WRVA Road in Henrico (Wikipedia).

Plan table lists WRXL as 'NP' (National Primary, FEMA NP facility, Facility ID 11961) and notes 'This NP station WRXL is also LP-2'. Alt rock 'Alt 102-1'; studios/transmitter on Basie Road (Wikipedia).

Listed as LP-3 in the EAS plan table (Facility ID 11914), listed first-alerting source WRXL. 50 kW News/Talk, transmitter on WRVA Road in Henrico (Wikipedia). Best AM news/talk option and the station most likely to run storm coverage. Also relayed on 96.1 FM via translator W241AP (Midlothian).

publicSafety.system: Richmond/Henrico/Chesterfield Trunking System (RadioReference SID 556), shared with Chesterfield and Richmond
publicSafety.type: Motorola Type II SmartZone, 800 MHz, analog + P25 Common Air Interface (System ID 6F3A)
publicSafety.monitorable: Not by a scanner. RadioReference shows 18 of 20 Henrico PD talkgroups marked 'D Enc' (fully encrypted); only the B/E alarm data and an announcement talkgroup are clear. Data is volunteer-maintained and may lag reality.

publicSafety.type: Motorola Type II SmartZone, 800 MHz, analog + P25 CAI
publicSafety.monitorable: Per RadioReference, 0 of 28 Henrico Fire/EMS talkgroups are marked encrypted (Fire Disp 1/2, Tac 4-13, Special Ops, EMS Ops 8-10, etc.). A trunk-tracking P25-capable scanner is needed. Henrico site 001 has 16 frequencies. Check RadioReference for current talkgroup numbers; I did not copy them.

publicSafety.agency: Capital Region Radio System (Henrico, Chesterfield, Hanover, Richmond, Colonial Heights)
publicSafety.system: CRRS: replacement for the SmartZone system
publicSafety.monitorable: Not live yet as far as the opened sources show. A Nov 5, 2025 JEMS report says Henrico expects Motorola to finish in May 2028 (contract signed 2016); the RadioReference wiki still says 'approximately 2026'. Expect the current scanner-friendly system to be replaced and Phase II needs a Phase II-capable scanner. Encryption policy on the new system is not stated anywhere I opened.

publicSafety.agency: Virginia State Police and other state agencies (STARS)
publicSafety.type: P25 Phase II trunked (System ID 19E); mostly 151-162 MHz sites plus 851-853 MHz mobile sites per RadioReference
publicSafety.monitorable: RadioReference shows all 116 listed Virginia State Police talkgroups with the Enc flag, so VSP is not monitorable. Other state agencies (VDOT, Corrections, DMV, Wildlife Resources, etc.) have talkgroups, not all analyzed. Richmond-area sites include Glen Allen (Henrico) and Richmond (Chesterfield). VSP's page confirms STARS supports Over-the-Air Re-Keying for encryption.

communities.name: VAMesh (Richmond / Central region)
communities.area: Virginia statewide; Richmond/Central listed as 'Expanding' interconnect region
communities.notes: IMPORTANT: VAMesh is built on MeshCore, which cannot talk directly to Meshtastic nodes. Richmond is not a priority build area yet. Contact info@vamesh.com.

meshtastic.notes: Meshtastic's local-groups page (opened) lists only MadisonMesh, Albemarle Mesh and Virginia Peninsula Mesh in Virginia plus DMV Mesh on Reddit; none is in Richmond. Region US = 902.0-928.0 MHz, default preset LONG_FAST, slot 0 picks frequency by channel-name hash (meshtastic.org LoRa docs). A node first configured from its own screen may start on LONG_TURBO, which will not talk to LongFast nodes.

fccRules.summary: Any amateur can use any means at hand to get help when life or property is in immediate danger and normal communications are down; no other amateur rule blocks this emergency use.
A station in distress may use any means to signal for help, report its location and get assistance, and other stations may use their equipment to help it.

RACES: only stations registered with a civil defense organization, run by licensed operators enrolled with it, and every transmission needs approval of the civil defense body for that area. Routine drills are limited to 1 hour a week.
FRS has 22 channels, each 12.5 kHz wide, shared with GMRS.
FRS power: ERP at or below 0.5 W on channels 8-14; at or below 2 W on channels 1-7 and 15-22.

GMRS has 30 channels (16 main, 14 interstitial) listed by frequency, with different allowed station types per group; 467 MHz main channels are for mobile/handheld/control only through a repeater or brief tests.
GMRS power: 50 W transmitter output for mobile/repeater/base on main channels, 15 W fixed; 462 MHz interstitial 5 W ERP; 467 MHz interstitial 0.5 W ERP.
MURS has five channels (151.820, 151.880, 151.940, 154.570, 154.600 MHz) with a 2 W power limit.
